subject: Re: Streaming model fit & UX follow-up — Acme Health
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Demo follow-up + streaming concerns

Thanks again for the demo today — Kelsey and I appreciated the walkthrough. A couple of follow-ups from our side: 

- We saw intermittent partial outputs in the streaming demo (sentences cutting off mid-thought). This breaks our clinician UX.
- Latency at the 95th percentile looked higher than we'd hoped on long notes (~1.2s/token).
- We're sensitive to hallucinations in clinical context; need a model/recommendation for best fit (accuracy vs cost).

Can you send a short plan for an eval we can run against our prompt sets + a recommendation of 1-2 models to try? Also, any quick mitigation for the streaming partial-output issue would be helpful while we evaluate.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Clinical AI
Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmehealth.com>, Kelsey Nguyen <kelsey@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + streaming concerns

Samir / Kelsey — great meeting, thanks for the clear notes. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Recap: 
- Problem: partial streaming outputs (coherence cutoffs) + 95p latency concerns on long clinical notes.
- Risk: hallucination exposure on sensitive entities.

Proposed next steps (suggested timeline):
1) Short eval run (we can run on our infra or you can run locally) using your 100 representative prompt-set + 50 long-note stress tests — goal: accuracy, hallucination rate, and streaming coherence metrics. Target: 1 week for first pass.
2) Model recommendations + quantization profiles from our side (we'll include throughput/latency estimates and cost delta).
3) Short-term streaming mitigation: 1) adjust server-side stop-sequence heuristics, 2) increase small-response prefix buffering to avoid mid-sentence cuts (low-risk change), 3) try a larger context model for critical endpoints if latency budget allows.

I've looped in Jordan (model fit) and Dev (streaming infra) to scope the eval and mitigation work. I'll share an eval plan + Drive folder by EOD tomorrow. If you want to accelerate, we can schedule a 30-minute technical sync next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Demo follow-up + streaming concerns — action items

Jordan / Dev — forwarding Acme's notes. Please see requested deliverables: 

A) Jordan: model recommendations (2 tiers: high-accuracy, cost-optimized) + a suggested prompt set tweak for stop sequences and guardrails. Include benchmark links and expected 95p latency for our Dedicated configs. Attach a short PDF that summarizes tradeoffs.

B) Dev: quick streaming mitigations we can ship on Redwood-hosted endpoints: 
   - Increase prefix buffering to 150-200ms for long-response endpoints (low-risk).
   - Server-side stop-sequence enforcement: add an aggressive fallback that waits for final punctuation before flushing partial tokens when enabled.
   - Add telemetry flags to capture partial-output events so we can measure improvement.

Target: internal draft by Mon EOD (9 Nov). I'll consolidate and send to Acme on Tues morning.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Demo follow-up + streaming concerns — action items

Marissa — quick model-fit summary attached (redwood_model_recommendations.pdf) and a short CSV with eval seeds (acme_health_eval_results.csv). TL;DR: 

- Tier 1 (accuracy-first): Redwood-XL-3B (float16 / 8-bit dynamic quant) — best hallucination profile on clinical prompts in our tests, expected 95p latency: ~0.95s/token on Dedicated A100 pool; higher unit cost.
- Tier 2 (cost-optimized): Redwood-Large-1.4B (int8 quant) — slightly higher hallucination rate on complex entity tasks but acceptable for triage workflows; 95p latency: ~0.65s/token with good batching.

Streaming UX notes from eval: 
- Partial-output events correlate with short server flush windows and insufficient lookahead on stop-sequence heuristics. Samples attached (streaming_examples.mov) show mid-sentence cuts mostly when responses contain long lists or parentheses.
- Short-term mitigation validated locally: prefix buffering + punctuation-aware flush reduced partial outputs by ~70% on our sample set. Implementation cost: minor infra change + feature flag.

Recommendations: 
1) Run Acme's 100-prompt suite against both tiers (we can run if they share anonymized prompts).
2) Toggle prefix buffering + punctuation flush in a canary for 48-72h and measure partial-output events.
3) If hallucination sensitivity remains, move critical endpoints to Tier 1 models and keep others on Tier 2.

Links / artifacts: 
- Eval notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFGH-acme-evals
- Internal perf report: https://redwood-internal/reports/acme_evals/2026-11-09

I'll assemble a short PDF summary for Acme and include the performance/cost table. Dev — see inline for infra change notes.

— Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmehealth.com>, Kelsey Nguyen <kelsey@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Streaming model fit & UX follow-up — Acme Health (plan + next steps)

Samir / Kelsey — attaching the model recommendation summary and a small set of eval artifacts (see attachments). Concrete next steps: 

1) Eval run: we can run the 100 prompt + 50 long-note stress tests for you this week. Please upload anonymized prompts to the Drive folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFGH-acme-evals by EOD Wed (11 Nov). Estimated turnaround: 4 business days for first pass.

2) Streaming mitigation (canary): Dev will enable prefix buffering + punctuation-aware flush on a canary endpoint for 72 hours. Expected customer impact: fewer partial outputs with negligible latency increase (~+50-120ms end-to-end). We will share telemetry dashboards after the canary.

3) Model split recommendation: If eval shows Tier 1 is materially better on hallucination-sensitive tasks, we recommend running critical clinician-facing paths on Tier 1 and batch/triage on Tier 2. We'll include expected cost impacts in the final report.

Please confirm if you'd like Redwood to run the eval (we'll need the anonymized prompts + a small sample of production long notes) or if you prefer to run locally with our eval scripts. Also propose two 30-minute slots next week for a technical sync — Wed 11/11 10:00-10:30 PT or Thu 11/12 13:00-13:30 PT.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Mobile: (415) 555-0123
